codeReview.summary: Implementation is correct and complete. synthesizeWorkerResult now detects report_result tool_execution_end events via extractHandoffArgs(), validates the handoff structure via validateHandoff(), and populates WorkerResult.handoff on success. Missing report_result triggers failure in strict mode (default) or success-with-warning in legacy mode. Malformed data produces a descriptive failure rather than crashing. Flow ordering is correct: exit code and fatal tool errors are checked before handoff extraction, so crashes take precedence. All 5 changed files are consistent and well-tested with 18 new tests covering VAL-HANDOFF-002 through VAL-HANDOFF-009. Integration tests in integration.test.ts and advanced-integration.test.ts were properly updated to include report_result in mock worker outputs.

issues.description: validSeverities set is defined inside validateHandoff with hardcoded values ['low', 'medium', 'high'] that must stay in sync with the WorkerHandoff type union in types.ts (line 216). If the type changes, this set must be manually updated. This is consistent with existing patterns in the codebase, so not blocking.

extractHandoffArgs returns the first report_result event found. If a worker somehow calls report_result multiple times, only the first call's data is used. This is reasonable behavior but undocumented. The last call might be more appropriate if the worker corrects itself, though this is an unlikely edge case.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker correctly used the pattern of not passing options to synthesizeWorkerResult in spawn-worker.ts, making strict mode the default. This convention (strict-by-default for report_result) should be noted since new callers of synthesizeWorkerResult need to know whether to pass legacyMode.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: extensions/tools/spawn-worker.ts:803 calls synthesizeWorkerResult without options parameter, defaulting to strict mode per VAL-HANDOFF-008

summary: Feature passes review. The implementation correctly adds handoff extraction from report_result events in the NDJSON stream, with proper strict/legacy mode handling, structural validation, and graceful error handling for malformed data. All expected behaviors from the validation contract (VAL-HANDOFF-002 through VAL-HANDOFF-009) are covered by tests. Integration tests were properly updated. Two non-blocking observations noted: hardcoded severity set that must stay in sync with the type, and first-match semantics for multiple report_result calls.
